prompt:
Use case: illustration-story / source-faithful narrative style transfer.
Create ONE finished SQUARE opaque story illustration for C01-CH03-S11, the silent cemetery name-record scene. Native 1254 x 1254 preferred. Preserve a complete square authored canvas intended to downsample to canonical 128 x 128. Do not make a landscape image or crop into 16:9. No border or panels.
REFERENCES: Image1 is the exact original source cell and authority for the cemetery's identity and spatial ingredients. Image2 is approved chunky matte cartoon style only; do not copy its bridges, river, soldiers or combat. This is a complete cemetery environment, NEVER an isolated pile of name tags.
SCENE AND ORIGINAL IDENTITY: Elevated three-quarter view into a small walled old cemetery among dark evergreen and broad rust-orange autumn trees, with faceted gray rocks behind. A low gray stone boundary with restrained iron railing, an iron entrance gate centered near the bottom, a small slate-roofed caretaker shelter just outside the lower-left wall, a large hooded memorial statue on a square stone pedestal slightly above center. Multiple individual gray headstones with low grave slabs border broad readable stone paths. Several modest warm lanterns on short stone posts. The scene remains a full graveyard with statue, graves, paths, gate, fence, people and autumn woodland, not a religious boss arena or souvenir display.
NARRATIVE ACTION: The living carry their own names on plain pale wooden waist tags so their companions can recognize them among the cemetery's confused echoes. Individual dead people are remembered on separate grave markers. Show a modest quiet group of about eight anonymous adult travelers and caretakers working independently, not an army or a mass ceremony. Give three foremost people clearly visible pale rectangular wood tags hanging from belt cords. Near the center, a plain brown-cloaked adult kneels beside one upright headstone, carefully attaching a separate pale paper name strip to its face; a companion with a waist tag stands beside them holding two spare paper strips. Another caretaker farther back tends a different grave with a small warm lamp. Their varied poses convey practical remembrance, not worship or synchronous kneeling. Do not depict specific named protagonists or assert a choice-dependent story outcome. No child needs to appear. The name marks on tags and stones are only a few irregular abstract strokes, never readable invented names, lettering, numbers, runic words or heraldry. Tags are mundane records, not magic talismans. Keep waist tags separate from grave markers.
COMPOSITION: Use a simplified version of the original cemetery plan. Roughly eight to ten substantial headstones, wide quiet paths, generous gaps between human silhouettes. Hooded statue and the central paper-at-grave interaction together create the main vertical focus. Keep the three foreground waist tags, central headstone work and the complete memorial statue well inside the central half of the image; gate centered below. Important objects and every human body are complete within the square. Trees may continue naturally beyond edges. Nothing presented as cutout sprites. Preserve graveyard setting at tiny canonical size, with strong visual hierarchy rather than lots of miniature detail.
STYLE AND MOOD: Approved exaggerated chunky matte cartoon family. Bold stable contours, broad planes, thick slate masonry and simple rounded cloth, 2-3 flat shades per material, grouped foliage masses, few large paving slabs. Reduce source density and microtexture severely. No leaf-speckle ground carpet, pebbles, fine cobbles, hatch shading, scratches, intricate filigree, photographic rendering or glossy metal. Calm cool dusk with restrained warm amber lanterns and pale name tags; sufficient midtone clarity for 128-pixel reading. Quiet humane remembrance, faint chill, not cute celebration or lurid horror. Blue-gray stone, muted olive/brown clothing, rust-orange foliage and warm cream record strips. Lantern light stays localized, no glowing tags or supernatural beams.
CONSTRAINTS: One intentionally opaque complete cemetery scene. No checkerboard, transparent exterior, isolated prop montage, giant close-up name-tag emblem, extra panels, captions, UI, watermark, symbols or readable text. No living dragon, skeleton army, crowns, flags or new heraldry. No aspect or gameplay changes. The source's graveyard identity and the living-waist-tag versus individual-grave-name relationship must both remain clear.
